title: Closing-Month Refund Calculation — Collateral Protection Insurance Premium Refund by Check
content:
The closing-month refund under Collateral Protection Insurance is the charge's premium multiplied by its refundable days and divided by its period days, rounded half-up to the cent. The refund carries no interest, fee or credit, and a mailed refund below the product's smallest check amount is not issued.

## The charge

The charge the closing-month refund refunds is the capitalised premium charge on the record (billed as added to the contract balance) with the latest billing period start. Its premium is the sum of the capitalised premium charged for that billing period, and its period days are the calendar days from its billing period start through its billing period end, both days counted.

## The proofs read

The proofs the closing-month refund reads are taken from every arrival channel alike — the insurer's electronic feed, an insurer fax, an insurance agent call and a declarations page upload, binder or declarations page: for each channel, the record's one accepted proof of that channel, if any. The channel decides only which rule reviewed a proof, never how its days count.

- A proof **counts** for the period when its expiration date falls on or after the period start.
- A counting proof **reaches the covered stretch** when it also took effect on or before the closed date.
- A reaching proof's **span** runs from the later of the period start and its effective date through the earlier of its expiration date and the closed date.

## Refund basis and refundable days

| Records show | Refund basis | Refundable days |
|---|---|---|
| a counting proof that took effect on or before the record's placement effective date | full, no lapse | every day of the period |
| otherwise, no counting proof reaching the covered stretch | pro rata from closure | the post-closing days |
| otherwise | pro rata from proof effective | the covered days added to the post-closing days |

A counting proof that took effect on or before the placement effective date means the borrower's own coverage ran with no gap from the placed coverage's effective date into the period; an insurer's reinstatement of the policy on file without a gap is such a proof, the product accepting retroactive reinstatement.

The **covered days** are the days of the period from the latest policy effective date among the reaching proofs through the closed date, both ends counted. A charge whose period ends on the closed date has no post-closing days.

## Hypothetical calculation

Take hypothetical figures: a capitalised premium of USD 100.00 for a 30-day period, days 1 to 30, on a record closed on day 30, placed coverage having taken effect before the period, and one accepted proof that took effect on day 21 and expires after the period. The proof counts and reaches the covered stretch, so the basis is pro rata from proof effective. Covered days run from day 21 through day 30, 10 days, and there are no post-closing days. The refund is USD 100.00 multiplied by 10 and divided by 30, USD 33.333, rounded half-up to USD 33.33.
